reason: The observation checks out; the fix does not, and the fix is the finding. Driven at state=day, 1440 and 390: the Behind you details is closed (details.open === false), the section's innerText is exactly "BEHIND YOU / 9 moments / Venue walk-through, 19 September.", and nothing but the footer chrome (Kept by Orla / Signal Timeline) sits below it. So yes, the morning's last content line is a note about a fortnight-old site visit. But the proposed replacement is copy the record cannot produce. The earliest past item's title in fixture.js is "We said yes" — the couple's own first-person words. "It began on 2 January, when you said yes." requires a person shift (We→you), a case fold, and a hand-written frame ("It began on … when …") that exists nowhere in the artifact. The seat's own justification is false on the code: the grammar that sentence already uses is title + ", " + fmt.medium(date) + "." (render-b.js:315), and the accessor it already calls would yield "We said yes, 2 January.", not the seat's string. The only case transform the file performs anywhere is a lowercase-first on the cancelled title (render-b.js:321). Worse, the invented sentence only parses because this one fixture's earliest title happens to be a first-person past-tense verb phrase; a project whose first moment reads "The Orchard reserved" yields "It began on 18 April, when you the Orchard reserved." That is a demo trick, not a rule, in an artifact whose stated discipline (fixture.js header, LANGUAGE.md) is that every string on every surface derives from one accessor — exactly the credibility the fixture header says a hand-written line spends. And the derivable version still costs coherence: the folded sentence would name the LAST row of a disclosure whose accessible label is "Behind you, most recent first" and whose lead row is the walk-through at 14 days back, so a reader who taps + to find the line they just read is sent 274 days to the bottom of the rail. On every other state the folded sentence names the row the opened list leads with, and the artifact has already been through one round of fixing precisely this summary/list relationship (the b-behindNote comment on printing a title visible twelve pixels below it). The morning also already carries its written line, "This is the day the plan was for.", in the optical centre of the composition, which the finding concedes. Real observation, unbuildable fix, net regression on the buildable version — refuted.
sharpenedFix: If a future round wants to reopen this, the only honest version is derivable and small: on the day clock only, keep the existing grammar and swap the subject to the first non-cancelled past item — done[0].title + ", " + F.fmt.medium(done[0].date) + "." → "We said yes, 2 January." — and, to pay the coherence cost, reverse the day-state backMeasure to run oldest-first with its aria-label changed to match, so the sentence still names the row the disclosure leads with. That is a build with a behaviour-gate consequence, not a copy edit, and it should not land unverified in a final round.
